AXP.rationale: American Express demonstrates strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 results showed 11% revenue growth YoY to $18.9B, 18% EPS growth to $4.28, and 35% ROE — all beating consensus estimates. The quarterly trajectory shows consistent sequential improvement: revenue from $9.63B (Q1 2025) to $10.52B (Q1 2026), and EPS from $3.64 to $4.28. The closed-loop business, premium customer focus, and strong brand create a durable competitive moat. Balance sheet is sound with CET1 at 10.5% and $53.8B cash. Credit metrics are stable (2.3% net write-off rate, 1.3% delinquency). Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance of 9-10% revenue growth and $17.30-$17.90 EPS, signaling confidence. On valuation, the current P/E of 19.5x sits near the low end of its 12-month range (18.1-25.3x), having compressed from ~24-25x in late 2025 as the stock declined 13.4% over the past quarter. P/B of 6.4x is also near the bottom of its 6.0-8.2x range. This suggests the market is paying less for the same or better earnings power versus recent history. The Q1 earnings beat (EPS $4.28 vs ~$4.00-4.06 consensus) reported on April 23 provides a near-term catalyst, though the stock dipped slightly post-earnings, suggesting the beat may not be fully priced. Risks include macro/consumer spending sensitivity, geopolitical tensions affecting travel, and regulatory pressure on interchange fees. The elevated VIX (19.3) and rising oil prices ($99/bbl) create headwinds for discretionary spending. Overall, a high-quality franchise trading at a reasonable discount to its recent history with solid execution, warranting a moderately positive score.
